title: Why Compute Still Trades in Group Chats — Affaan Mustafa & Alejandro Soumah Fernandez, Jump Trading
talk_summary: A market-structure talk about how physical GPU capacity is traded OTC in private chats, why contracts are bespoke and non-fungible, and how financing/prepayment mismatches constrain growing companies. It is about compute procurement and hedging, not about building or running AI agents.

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue every compute deal is bespoke (spec sheets, BOM vs delivery, ambiguous terms like 'memory'), so buyers can't compare offers; they propose standard capacity contracts, common specs and terms to make capacity comparable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every deal is bespoke. There's different spec sheets, there's formats. The bill of materials may not match the actual like delivery

takeaways.technique: On-demand bridging of capacity gaps vs long commitments
takeaways.what_they_do: They describe using on-demand capacity to bridge shortfalls between committed blocks, and comparing the yield of financing a prepayment against just buying on-demand at the time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: do you use on demand to close the area under the gap and bridge the shortfall?
